web_title: 4. The Regulatory Clock, Substitutes & Helium Supply
question: Which rules and supply chains decide how long this company's main products stay the main products?

epigraph.quote: Adopted in 2016, the Amendment commits countries to reducing HFC production and consumption with differentiated timelines for developed and developing nations.
epigraph.author: UNEP Ozone Secretariat, Kigali Amendment overview [17]

web_blocks.html: Refrigerant gas is regulated before it is sold. The rules that shape this company’s product mix are not set in a boardroom. They sit in an international treaty, and the treaty decides how fast the company’s main molecules must shrink. This chapter reads the treaty as a supply rule for this business, then tests the helium supply chain, which has its own limits.

web_blocks.title: The Montreal Protocol and the Kigali Amendment

web_blocks.html: The Montreal Protocol is the treaty that phased out the ozone-depleting gases. The Kigali Amendment extended the framework to hydrofluorocarbons, the HFCs that replaced the older gases. The UNEP summary puts it plainly: “Adopted in 2016, the Amendment commits countries to reducing HFC production and consumption with differentiated timelines for developed and developing nations.” [17] Developed countries began their reductions in 2019 [17]. HFCs do not deplete the ozone layer, but they are potent greenhouse gases, and that is why they now sit under a timetable.

web_blocks.title: Where India sits in the schedule

web_blocks.html: India is in Group 2 of the HFC annex, with Bahrain, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates [16]. For Group 2 the base level is the average HFC consumption for 2024 to 2026 plus 65% of the HCFC baseline. The freeze takes effect on 1 January 2028 [16]. A freeze caps consumption at the base level, so the national ceiling is set by the years that are happening now.

The treaty summary does not say how India will share its national ceiling among companies, and no formal allocation rule has been notified yet (expected in 2027). On the 19 November 2026 earnings call, management confirmed that the 2024–2026 baseline window is already distorting the market: importers are aggressively maximizing volumes before the baseline closes to lock in 20-year entitlements, creating severe selling pressure that hit Q2 FY27 spreads [36]. Management asserted that Stallion expects to receive “more than 50% of the country quota” and lift regular-business PAT margins from 10% to 15% after 2028—an unverified forward expectation until the government publishes company-level allocations [36].

R-32 is an HFC. The FY25 annual report records a partnership with Daikin for HFC-32 sourcing [4]. So the company’s largest product, and the planned Bhilwara R-32 plant, both sit inside the freeze rather than outside it [2][9].

web_blocks.title: Trade remedies: DGTR’s five-year anti-dumping renewal on Chinese R-32

web_blocks.html: A second regulatory layer omitted from the initial baseline analysis is India’s trade-remedy shield on Chinese R-32 [41]. India originally imposed anti-dumping duty (ADD) on Chinese HFC Component R-32 in December 2021 (Notification No. 75/2021-Customs (ADD)) [41]. On 18 September 2026, following a sunset review initiated on an application by SRF Limited and supported by Gujarat Fluorochemicals (10,000 MTPA R-32) and Navin Fluorine (9,000 MTPA at review [41]; 15,000 MTPA commercialized in November 2026 [42]), India’s Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) issued Final Findings in Case No. AD (SSR)-11/2025 recommending continuation of anti-dumping duty on Chinese R-32 imports for another five years (subject to Ministry of Finance customs notification) [41].

This ruling cuts asymmetrically across Stallion’s transition. While Bhilwara remains uncommissioned through Q1 FY28, Stallion is an importer reliant on China for over 90% of imported inputs—meaning continued ADD elevates landed costs while domestic producers SRF, GFL, and Navin Fluorine enjoy protected realizations [6][41]. Conversely, once Bhilwara begins producing in April–May 2027, prolonged ADD could support domestic R-32 pricing, though Stallion must still compete against roughly 80,000 tonnes of coming Indian R-32 capacity (against ~20,000 tonnes of domestic demand) without captive AHF backward integration [36][41].

The company is hedging the rule with lower-warming molecules. It supplies HFO-1234yf to Indian auto makers [4], and the redesigned Mambattu facility will blend HFO with R-32 once completed in January 2027 / Q1 FY28 [36][37]. However, on the 19 November 2026 call management confirmed that Bhilwara currently has no HFO manufacturing capability, Environmental Clearance for the proposed ₹200 crore Hurda HFO plant is still pending, funding remains undecided, and construction will not begin until three to five months after Bhilwara R-32 stabilizes—pushing any HFO build into late 2027 at the earliest [36].

That stretches the timeline directly against the 1 January 2028 HFC freeze. Management estimated India’s current HFO demand at 500 to 600 tonnes, rising above 2,500 tonnes after 2028 [36]. Yet backward-integrated rivals are already executing commercial HFO lines: Navin Fluorine extended its Solstice Advanced Materials HFO contract (~$590 million) through December 2032 [42], and SRF is building a 20,000 MTPA fourth-generation refrigerant unit in Odisha [44]. Because Stallion’s Honeywell distribution relationship is non-exclusive and HFO patents are approaching expiry, Stallion does not hold an exclusive moat over India’s HFO transition [36].

On the August call, management said the company’s R-32 imports were over 4,000 tons before it began making R-32 itself, and that its own requirement would be roughly 40 to 50% of production [9]. That is a spoken figure, and I did not find it in a filing. It matters because it shows how much of the company’s refrigerant volume depends on what it can make itself, which is the point of the Bhilwara plant.

web_blocks.title: What to watch in the next filings

web_blocks.html: Four things will tell you more than any call. First, the Ministry of Finance customs notification following DGTR’s 18 September 2026 five-year R-32 ADD recommendation, because it directly shapes import spreads until Bhilwara stabilizes [41]. Second, the national HFC quota allocation when notified in 2027, to test management’s “over 50% country quota” claim [36]. Third, Environmental Clearance and funding terms for the Bhilwara HFO plant [36]. Fourth, quarterly Khalapur helium volumes, now that the 1,200 MTPA facility commenced operations on 21 September 2026 [36][37].

Keep the dates and the numbers in one place as you read. A regulatory date tells you when a product line must change. A capex line tells you whether the company can change in time. A volume line tells you whether the new plant is earning. The three together are the test of whether the substitute story is a plan or only a slide.

External Learning Hub. Check the regulatory and helium figures yourself. web_blocks.title: Helium: a supply chain built on other countries

web_blocks.html: The helium project is the company’s other new line, and its supply rests on partners rather than on owned resources. Commercial operations at the 1,200 MTPA Khalapur helium facility began on 21 September 2026. Liquid helium comes through Sharjah Oxygen Company in Dubai, which sources from RAS Gases & Oilfields in Qatar [1]. Helium is recovered as a by-product, so supply follows the producers’ output rather than the company’s demand [11], and as Q2 FY27’s Gulf freight and material disruptions illustrated, Middle East logistics bottlenecks directly affect landed costs.

The USGS summary gives United States helium import sources for 2021 to 2024: Canada 47%, Qatar 28%, Algeria 10%, China 5% and other sources 10% [21]. These are United States figures, not India’s, and the company’s own supply mix is not disclosed. They still show concentration in the global market, with a large share of helium flowing from two producers. The same summary puts the estimated 2025 base level for Grade-A helium at about $12 per cubic meter, or $330 per thousand cubic feet [21].

Management’s view of the helium volume is the reason to be careful. It expects the plant to run at about 20% of its 1,200 metric tons next year, not 50%, and says the ramp will be gradual [9]. A plant at a fifth of capacity has a partial revenue line, however strong the market is.

web_blocks.region_era: United States and global, FY2022 to FY2024, refrigerant substitution after the EU Mobile Air Conditioning Directive
web_blocks.mechanism: A regulation forced a change of refrigerant. The company had developed a lower-warming replacement in response to that rule, and its sales moved toward it while the legacy refrigerant line shrank.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Opteon refrigerant sales were $597 million in 2022, $710 million in 2023 and $810 million in 2024. Freon refrigerant sales over the same years were $750 million, $722 million and $614 million [27].
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Stallion faces the same kind of change. Its R-32 is an HFC that the treaty caps, so its HFO line has to grow fast enough to replace the volume the cap removes. With Bhilwara HFO construction now deferred until after R-32 stabilizes in late 2027, watch EC approvals, funding, and rival HFO ramps closely.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR’S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Put the three clocks side by side. The Kigali freeze arrives on 1 January 2028; DGTR’s five-year Chinese R-32 anti-dumping extension squeezes unintegrated imports right now; and Bhilwara’s HFO plant will not even break ground until three to five months after R-32 stabilizes in mid-2027, with EC and funding still pending.

Meanwhile, company-level India HFC quotas will not be known until 2027. Treat management’s claim of receiving over half the country quota as an unverified hope until the government publishes the formula.

book_paragraphs: Some of the rules that shape this company are not written by the company, or by its auditors, or even by the Indian government alone. They come from a treaty signed decades ago and amended since. The Montreal Protocol began as a way to phase out the gases that damage the ozone layer. The Kigali Amendment, adopted in 2016, brought in a second group of gases, the hydrofluorocarbons, which the company sells as refrigerants. Those gases do not harm the ozone layer, but they trap a lot of heat. So the treaty now limits how much of them the world can make and use, and it does so on a timetable.

The UNEP summary of Kigali says the amendment sets differentiated timelines for developed and developing nations. Developed countries started their reductions in 2019. India sits in Group 2, where the baseline is the average HFC consumption over 2024 to 2026 plus 65% of the older HCFC baseline, freezing on 1 January 2028. On the 19 November 2026 call, management confirmed that the closing months of the 2024–2026 baseline window are already triggering heavy import-and-dump selling across India as players chase 20-year quota entitlements. Management claims Stallion will receive more than 50% of India’s import quota when allocations are announced in 2027, lifting regular-business PAT margins to 15% after 2028—a claim that remains entirely unverified until the government publishes company quotas.

A second regulatory force missed in the original draft is India’s anti-dumping duty on Chinese R-32. Originally imposed in December 2021, the duty underwent a sunset review petitioned by SRF and supported by Gujarat Fluorochemicals and Navin Fluorine. On 18 September 2026, DGTR recommended extending the anti-dumping duty on Chinese R-32 for five more years. Until Bhilwara runs reliably in mid-2027, prolonged anti-dumping duties penalize an import-dependent blender like Stallion while bolstering the realizations of integrated domestic manufacturers.

The substitutes—HFOs—face a widening timing gap. Stallion supplies HFO-1234yf to Indian auto makers and redesigned Mambattu for HFO blending, now due in Q1 FY28. Yet Bhilwara currently has no HFO manufacturing capability. Management confirmed in November 2026 that environmental clearance is still pending, funding is undecided, and HFO plant construction will only begin three to five months after Bhilwara R-32 stabilizes—pushing ground-breaking to late 2027 at the earliest, right on top of the 2028 freeze. Meanwhile, Navin Fluorine has already extended its Solstice HFO contract to 2032, and SRF is building a 20,000-tonne fourth-generation refrigerant plant in Odisha.

The helium part of the business crossed an operational milestone when Khalapur’s 1,200 metric tonne facility commenced commercial operations on 21 September 2026. Liquid helium still arrives via a Dubai partner sourcing from Qatar, and as Q2 FY27’s Gulf material and freight disruptions proved, dependence on Middle East logistics carries real cost volatility. The USGS figures on global helium concentration remain useful context, and management’s cautious year-one guidance of about 20% utilization means helium will not rescue refrigerant spreads overnight.

Finally, look at Chemours in the United States. When European rules forced a shift away from older Freon refrigerants, Chemours had Opteon ready to capture the volume, growing Opteon from $597 million to $810 million over three years as Freon fell from $750 million to $614 million. Stallion’s HFO plan is the same kind of transition bet—except Stallion is building late, without exclusive patents, and behind far larger integrated Indian peers.

Keep three items on your regulatory checklist: the Ministry of Finance customs notification on Chinese R-32 anti-dumping duty, India’s 2027 company-level HFC quota allocation, and environmental clearance plus funding for Bhilwara’s HFO plant. Until all three are confirmed in public filings, treat post-2028 margin expansion as an unproven projection.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR’S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Put the two dates in one line. The freeze comes in 2028, and the substitute plant starts construction in 2027 and needs time to run. What does this company sell in the gap? If you cannot answer that from the filings, write the question down and keep it until the allocation rule is public.
